name: Human Factors in Design - 1
description: This course provides an intermediate level review of the principles of human factors/ergonomics with a focus human information processing and person-technology models in ergonomic design. The course will introduce students to how human factors/ergonomics can be systematically considered and implemented in the development of displays and interactions. The course covers origins of ergonomics, systems thinking, human error, human information processing; human-machine systems; information design; display and control design; affordances and natural mapping; principles of interaction design; inclusive design and accessibility; and design for disability and aging. Through lectures and course activities students will develop competencies in human factors/ergonomics and inclusive design for academic research and professional practice.
